pcs.pc_description: greet the customer (shipper/forwarder) in a courteous manner
gather the details of the shipment from the customer and provide the requirements applicable for general and special cargo and special products

obtain all the basic information from the customer, including SLI (Shipper’s Letter of Instruction), packing list, certificate of origin, commercial invoice, customs approval to export (let export) and other relevant documents where appropriate
check the system database, TACT rules and applicable manuals to ensure that the shipment is permitted to be carried without any restrictions or limitations
check the applicable tariff for the shipment
assess the applicable rate/charges, including other applicable charges such as Terminal Storage and Processing Charges (TSP), and documentation as per the tariff provided by the pricing section
assess the requirement for cargo insurance and, if necessary, acquire coverage to safeguard against loss or damage during transportation
check the packing to ensure cargo safety during transit. Highlight airline and international shipping requirements on packaging
provide the customer with the details of the rate/charge and the total cost of carriage based on the details provided by the customer and the applicable conditions, if any

make a booking with appropriate codes, where applicable, as per the optimum routing using the reservation system in case of free allocation by ensuring payment-related requirements are met by the customer
queue the booking to capacity optimization where the weight/volume of shipment booking requested by the customer exceeds free allocation limitations or within the blocked space allotments
advise the customer that the actual charges payable may vary if the actual weight/dimensions delivered at the air cargo terminal is at variance with the booked weight/dimensions
communicate the expected delivery time and transit details. Explain any potential delays or factors that might affect the delivery schedule
explain the customs clearance process at both the origin and destination airports to the customer. Advise on any additional documentation required for customs purposes.
apply volume weight or higher chargeable weight, where appropriate and explain the details, including its impact on the freight charges to the customer
collect the applicable charges by debit/credit card/cash or any other form of payment as approved by company procedures and issue receipt/equivalent document specified to the customer
issue cargo system Air Waybill as per IATA, national and company regulations to conform to IATA, national and company regulations, whether physical or e-Air Waybill
advise the customer the basic information of when, where and how the physical shipment needs to be delivered for transportation to its final destination
print/email the cargo booking details of the customer and AWB and hand it over/send it to the customer
initiate changes in the booking, when requested by the customer within the parameters and guidelines specified for effecting such changes

assess the type of special cargo being booked such as Valuable (VAL), Vulnerable (VUN), Live Animals (AVI), Human Remains (HUM), Dangerous Goods (DGR), Heavy Cargo (HEA), Odd sized cargo (ODD), Automobiles/Vehicles (VEH) and so on as well as the special products of the airline, where appropriate
ensure trained/approved person performs the booking function related to that specific type of special cargo which is planned to be booked

advise the applicable documentation, permit, physical condition of the shipment, security, safety, acceptance checklist related requirements as pre conditions required to be fulfilled by the customer prior to booking the specific type of special cargo and special products
obtain required information related to the type of special cargo/special products to be booked, including advance arrangements with the carrier, origin, transit and destination
check all the documents, information provided by the customer thoroughly to ensure that the special cargo can be carried to its final destination avoiding the chances of hold up
determine whether the shipment could be booked or not based on available information
queue the booking to capacity optimization with the exact information available related to the type of special cargo being booked
update the shipment record in the cargo system with the current status of the requirements related to special cargo shipments, including those fulfilled and pending

reiterate to the customer the list of requirements that have been fulfilled by the customer and those remaining to be fulfilled, especially at the cargo terminal when the special cargo shipment is delivered for transportation to its destination

advise the customer that the actual charges payable may vary if the actual weight/dimensions of the special cargo/special products delivered at the air cargo terminal are at variance with the booked weight/dimensions
apply volume weight or higher chargeable weight, where appropriate and explain the details, including its impact on the freight charges to the customer
assess the applicable rate/charges, including other applicable charges such as Terminal Storage and Processing Charges (TSP), documentation as per the tariff provided by the pricing section
collect the applicable charges by debit/credit card/cash or any other form of payment as approved by company procedures and issue receipt/equivalent document specified to the customer
issue cargo system air waybill as per IATA, national and company regulations to conform to IATA, national and company regulations, whether physical or e-air waybill

pcs.pc_description: gather details of the various types of customers and enter the details in ‘customer relationship management’ or equivalent system/database
prepare a matrix with service satisfaction related elements under the supervisor’s guidance on customer service irregularities
analyze the complaint received from operational/commercial units to identify the root cause
identify internal triggers responsible for any service irregularity/claims and advise concerned section to prevent recurrence
analyze potential approaches in case of service irregularities/claims caused by external factors and advise supervisor/manager of possible methods to be adopted
prepare background notes for presentation to supervisor/manager to meet with the aggrieved customer
initiate and recommend service recovery measures to assist supervisor/manager to convince the customer to continue his/her business demonstrating corrective measures proposed/taken
liaise with marketing/sales units to assess potential methods/measures of service recovery
assess the efficacy of the service recovery measures implemented based on lessons derived from earlier irregularities
report to senior management of areas requiring improvement in a proactive manner to prevent future
listen, record customer verbal and written complaint/s
acknowledge receipt of the complaint/s with a suitable response as per organizational procedures
apologize to the customer for the inconvenience and, where possible, provide the expected time taken for resolution of the problem in full or in part
liaise with concerned operational/commercial unit/s to identify the potential locations of missing shipment or any missing piece/s
prepare detailed summary to include cause/s that led to service irregularities in the case of individual transaction/shipment
assess the eligible level of compensation payable to customer at the transactional level based on company, industry, international regulations, standards and procedures
propose the level of compensation payable for the specific transaction-related claim to the supervisor
update the customer on the claim amount approved by the management and escalate if the customer is not satisfied with the amount approved.
follow up individual customer’s service irregularity related case and update the records accordingly

escalate to supervisor/manager in the case of any repeated service irregularity suffered by a particular customer or where the customer’s profile warrants a special considered view due to a potential adverse impact in the future.
prepare MIS report related to claims received, settled/pending, special approvals, performance of claims over a given period, including supporting information
close the files of resolved cases
